page_hint: Ch 15, opening scope note (first paragraph after 'The Architect's Question')
quoted_clause: ⌈344/35⌉ = 10 hosts at 40 rps, bounded below by the ~7-host prefill requirement — prefill compute then binds
observed: The '~7-host prefill requirement' is inconsistent with the book's own 35%-MFU prefill screen, which gives 19 hosts (case i), 21 (case iii), or 22 (case ii) at 40 rps. The figure 7 arises only from the 100%-MFU theoretical ceiling (368,000 ÷ 56,500 = 6.51 → ⌈6.51⌉ = 7), a different operating point than the 35%-MFU screen used in Ch 16/17/20. Additionally, the clause 'prefill compute then binds' is arithmetically wrong for 7 < 10 (KV would bind), and is only correct for 19 > 10 (prefill binds).
root_cause: The scope note was written using the 100%-MFU theoretical ceiling (56,500 tok/s) instead of the 35%-MFU planning screen (19,780 tok/s) that the rest of the book uses for the independent prefill compute screen. The 'prefill compute then binds' clause was written for the 19 > 10 case but the number was left at 7.
correction: Replace '~7-host prefill requirement — prefill compute then binds' with 'the independent prefill compute screen (35% MFU, case i) requires ⌈368,000/19,780⌉ = 19 hosts, so prefill compute binds and the fleet is 19 hosts, not 10.' Alternatively, if the 100%-MFU figure is intended as a theoretical bound, state it explicitly: 'the 100%-MFU theoretical prefill ceiling implies only ⌈368,000/56,500⌉ = 7 hosts, but the 35%-MFU planning screen (used in Ch 16/17) requires 19 hosts, so prefill compute binds at 19 > 10.'
acceptance_test: The scope note's prefill figure must match the 35%-MFU prefill screen (19/21/22) stated in Ch 16 §16.3 and Ch 17 §17.4, and the 'binds' clause must be consistent with the comparison (prefill > KV → prefill binds; prefill < KV → KV binds).

page_hint: Ch 16 §16.3, Mode 1, 'Per request' paragraph; also Ch 16 §16.3 'Feasible served-volume bound' paragraph
quoted_clause: 10 rps × 8 h × 3,600 s × 260 workdays ÷ 12 = 6,240,000 requests/month, not 24×7; request-active time is 173.33 h/month
observed: The formula is arithmetically correct (74,880,000/12 = 6,240,000) but the '÷ 12' is unexplained. A reader sees '260 workdays' (an annual figure) multiplied by '8 h' (a daily figure) and then divided by 12 without being told that 260 is per-year and ÷12 converts to per-month. The resulting '173.33 h/month' active time (≈ 21.7 business days × 8 h) is consistent, but the formula as written looks like an arbitrary adjustment.
evidence: 260 workdays/year ÷ 12 months/year = 21.67 workdays/month. 21.67 × 8 h × 3,600 s/h = 624,096 s ≈ 624,000 s. 10 rps × 624,000 s = 6,240,000 req/mo. The '÷ 12' is the year-to-month conversion.
root_cause: The formula compresses two steps (annual-to-monthly conversion, then rate × time) into one line without labeling the '÷ 12' as a unit conversion.
correction: Rewrite as: '10 rps × 8 h/day × 3,600 s/h × (260 workdays/yr ÷ 12 mo/yr) = 10 × 8 × 3,600 × 21.67 ≈ 6,240,000 requests/month (active business-hours window; 173.33 h/mo of 8-h days, not 24×7).' Or simply: '10 rps × 173.33 h/mo × 3,600 s/h = 6,240,000 requests/month, where 173.33 h = 8 h × 21.67 business days (260/12).'
acceptance_test: A reader who does not know the canonical workload should be able to follow the derivation of 6,240,000 from the stated inputs without guessing what '÷ 12' represents.

quoted_clause: 2 rps average is 0.25 rps/replica, well inside the 0.48 rps/replica the canonical 21-host fleet sustains at its 40 rps peak
observed: The '0.48 rps/replica' figure is not derived in the text. The canonical fleet runs one 70B model per 8×H100 host (TP=8), so there is 1 model instance per host, giving 40/21 = 1.90 rps/host. The 0.48 figure appears to be 40/(21×4) = 0.476, implying 4 'replicas' per host (2 GPUs each), which contradicts the canonical 8-GPU tensor-parallel deployment. The mini-case's own setup ('2 GPUs per replica → 8 replicas across the two hosts') uses a different parallelism than the canonical, making the cross-reference to 'the canonical 21-host fleet' ambiguous.
evidence: 40 rps / 21 hosts = 1.90 rps/host (1 model instance per host in canonical TP=8). 40 / (21 × 4) = 0.476 ≈ 0.48 (4 replicas of 2 GPUs per host — not the canonical configuration). The mini-case's '2 GPUs per replica' is a different deployment shape.
root_cause: The comparison was made at the 'replica' granularity (2 GPUs) rather than the 'host' or 'model instance' granularity, and the canonical fleet's replica count was not stated.
correction: Either (a) restate the comparison at host level: '2 rps average is 1 rps/host across the two hosts, well inside the 40/21 ≈ 1.9 rps/host the canonical 21-host fleet sustains at peak'; or (b) if keeping the replica-level comparison, explicitly state: 'the canonical 21-host fleet, if reconfigured as 4 two-GPU replicas per host (84 replicas total), sustains 40/84 ≈ 0.48 rps/replica at peak — the mini-case's 0.25 rps/replica is within that.' Option (a) is simpler and avoids the configuration mismatch.
acceptance_test: The reader can verify the 0.48 (or 1.9) figure from the stated fleet size and arrival rate without inferring an unstated replica-per-host count.

quoted_clause: the per-host decode token rate ≈ B × HBM_BW ÷ weight_bytes, capped by compute and KV — at batch 1 that is ~239 tok/s, at batch 100 ~23,900 tok/s
observed: The formula is labeled 'per-host' but the numbers (239 tok/s at batch 1 for a 14 GB model) correspond to a single GPU (3.35 TB/s ÷ 14 GB = 239 tok/s), not an 8-GPU host (26.8 TB/s ÷ 14 GB = 1,914 tok/s). The counter-scenario implicitly assumes the 7B model runs on 1 GPU, but the 'per-host' label suggests 8 GPUs.
evidence: 1 GPU: 3.35×10¹² / 14×10⁹ = 239 tok/s. 8 GPUs: 8×3.35×10¹² / 14×10⁹ = 1,914 tok/s. The text's 239 matches the 1-GPU case.
root_cause: The counter-scenario uses a 7B model that fits on one GPU, but the formula's 'per-host' label was carried over from the canonical 8×H100 context without adjustment.
correction: Change 'per-host decode token rate' to 'per-GPU decode token rate (the 7B model fits on a single GPU; a host with 8 such GPUs would run 8 independent instances)' or simply 'per-instance decode token rate.' Add a brief note that the 7B model occupies 1 of the 8 GPUs, so the host can run 8 independent 7B instances.
acceptance_test: A reader computing 8 × 3.35 TB/s ÷ 14 GB gets 1,914 tok/s and does not find a contradiction with the stated 239 tok/s, because the per-GPU scope is explicit.

observed: The ceiling function ⌈344/17⌉ = ⌈20.235⌉ = 21 exactly. The tilde (~) implies approximation where the result is a precise integer from a defined operation.
root_cause: Carryover from a draft where the calculation was less precise, or a stylistic habit of hedging integer results.

quoted_clause: 436 GB ÷ (2.62 MB/token × 9,500 tokens) = 17.51 → floor 17 (conservative by one host: 344 ÷ 17.516 = 19.64 → 20 unrounded)
observed: The same quantity is given as '17.51' in the main clause and '17.516' in the parenthetical. The exact value is 436/24.9037 = 17.507. Neither 17.51 nor 17.516 is the exact value; they are different roundings of the same quantity, which creates a minor inconsistency within one sentence.
evidence: 2.62144 MB × 9,500 = 24,903.68 MB = 24.90368 GB. 436/24.90368 = 17.5074. Rounded to 2 dp: 17.51. Rounded to 3 dp: 17.507. The '17.516' does not match either standard rounding.
root_cause: The '17.516' appears to be a typo (transposition of 17.507 or 17.51 with an extra digit).
correction: Unify to '17.51' (or '17.507') in both places: '436 GB ÷ 24.9037 GB = 17.51 → floor 17 (conservative by one host: 344 ÷ 17.51 = 19.65 → 20 unrounded).'
acceptance_test: The same decimal representation of C appears in both the main clause and the parenthetical; no reader can identify two different values for the same quantity.
